text_blocks.snippet: Yes, OTC (over-the-counter) COVID-19 tests are generally accurate, particularly when used by individuals with symptoms, according to Harvard Health and the FDA. They are designed to detect an active COVID-19 infection. However, these tests, which are typically antigen tests, are less sensitive than molecular tests like PCR and may not detect the virus as early in an infection or in individuals without symptoms.

list.title: Accuracy with Symptoms:
list.snippet: At-home COVID tests are more effective at detecting the virus when individuals are experiencing symptoms. A study found that BinaxNow COVID tests detected nearly 90% of COVID cases when people had symptoms.

list.title: Lower Sensitivity for Asymptomatic Cases:
list.snippet: OTC tests are less accurate at detecting asymptomatic infections. They may only detect about half of asymptomatic cases.

list.title: Antigen vs. Molecular Tests:
list.snippet: Antigen tests, like most OTC tests, are generally less sensitive than molecular tests (like PCR). This means they are more likely to produce a false negative result, especially early in an infection or in asymptomatic individuals.

list.title: Importance of Repeat Testing:
list.snippet: The FDA recommends repeat testing following a negative result on an antigen test, especially if symptoms persist or if there is a high level of suspicion for COVID-19.

list.title: Follow Instructions Carefully:
list.snippet: It's crucial to follow the instructions provided with the specific at-home test kit carefully to ensure accurate results.
